text: Starting today, you can use Claude artifacts to create, run, and share desktop apps. The "Install as app" feature is rolling out in beta in Claude for Mac and Windows. When an artifact is installed as a Mac or Windows app, it gets its own icon and opens in its own window instead of inside Claude. You can share it with others, and it needs your permission before it can interact with your computer. You choose how much to allow. Each app can use Claude and your connectors, and it updates automatically when the underlying artifact is edited. This simplifies the process for building and maintaining apps for both knowledge workers and developers. Requests the app makes to Claude count toward your plan’s usage limits. Artifacts started out as a work output you’d share, like a chart or a webpage. People now use them as tools for everyday work, like a meeting prep page that regularly pulls from their calendar and email, or a tracker for the orders that need to ship that day. If you rely on a tool for work, it should open like the rest of your apps and remind you when something needs your attention. Installed apps can send notifications or add items to your menu bar or system tray. You choose permissions for each app, and Team and Enterprise admins can turn app permissions and full access on or off for their organization. People at Anthropic have used these to make: You can see more demo apps made by one of our engineers here (opens in new tab) . There are three levels of permissions: Your permission only covers the current version of the app, so Claude asks again after every update, even your own edits. If part of an app comes from another website, that part can change without Claude asking you again. You can only give full access to apps you made or, on Team and Enterprise, apps made by people in your organization. Anthropic doesn’t review apps before you install them, so only give full access to apps you trust. Describe your app to Claude, try it as an artifact, and then click "Install as app." You don’t have to package or sign it, and it uses your Claude account, so there’s no API key or separate login. Install as app is rolling out in beta on all plans. HIPAA-ready organizations and hybrid deployments can’t use it. It’s on by default for Team, with full access off. On Enterprise, it’s off until an owner turns it on. You need to be online and signed in to Claude to open an app. Some artifacts can’t be installed, including Claude Docs, Slides, and Sheets. Update Claude for Mac or Windows, open an artifact you use every day, and choose "Install as app" from the Share menu. Open a pull request and get back to building. Claude can now review pull requests, fix them, and approve the ones that a team's policy allows.
